evidence.quote: OAuth 2.0 allows users to log into their QuickBooks account via the OAuth 2.0 flow.
Each entity supports full and sparse update operations
QuickBooks Online imposes rate limits to restrict the number of requests in a specified timeframe.

result.notes: developer.intuit.com is a JS-rendered SPA that WebFetch could not extract text from (pages returned as truncated/empty), so auth/getting-started claims lean on the unauthenticated API probe (401 + WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm=\"Intuit\", confirming OAuth2 bearer tokens) and secondary sources (Intuit's own Medium/help-article summaries, getknit.dev) rather than a directly quoted primary page. Multiple independent secondary sources consistently describe: free self-serve signup at developer.intuit.com, automatic sandbox company creation (up to 5 per account), OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow exclusively (no API keys/basic auth), Client ID/Secret issued per app, and a rate limit around 500 req/min/company. QuickBooks spans multiple APIs (Accounting ~30 entities with CRUD+query, Payments, Payroll, Reports), pushing combined endpoint count into the hundreds (Composio wraps 114 discrete tools alone), hence "large". MCP support is community-only (caribooks/quickbooks, NyxToolsDev/quickbooks-mcp-server on registries); no official Intuit-published MCP server found. Confidence lowered because the primary developer.intuit.com pages could not be directly fetched/quoted within this pass.
result.one_liner: QuickBooks Online is Intuit's cloud accounting platform, exposing a REST Accounting API (plus separate Payments and Payroll APIs) for invoices, expenses, customers, and financial reporting.
